taxonomyNote: Nicholson (2025) via NatureServe retains North American Racer in Coluber while placing the striped, whip and coachwhip snakes in Masticophis; some sources give 'Eastern Racer'.
fieldMarks: Slender, smooth-scaled snake 90-190 cm long with a narrow head wider than the neck and distinct brow ridges.
Adults are uniformly dark above (black, bluish, grey or olive-brown) with a white to yellow chin and throat and a varied belly; 17 scale rows at midbody.
Divided anal plate; male tail is longer with a wide base, female tail tapers abruptly.
Juveniles are strongly patterned in grey, brown and red, fading at about 30 in.
behavior: Diurnal and fast; flees to burrows, thick vegetation or low branches, but if cornered coils, strikes and vibrates its tail.
Inactive in cold weather and dormant roughly October-March over much of its range; adults often hibernate communally.
Broad carnivorous diet: insects, frogs, lizards, small rodents and nestling birds; does not constrict prey.
habitat: Dry sunny areas with cover: old fields, open woodland, hedgerows, thickets and woodland edges; also deserts, prairies, sandhills, canyons and streamsides.
Climbs shrubs and small trees; absent from the driest deserts and subalpine zones.
range: Southern British Columbia, southern Saskatchewan, southern Ontario and southern Maine south through most of the United States (to southern California, Arizona, Texas and Florida) and into Mexico, Guatemala and Belize.
